knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_sbm"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12099> (open access, PMC4961079)
* Models:
  * `AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_sbm`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_sbm"))$description`
  * `AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_ded`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_ded"))$description`

Naloxegol is a peripherally acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist (a PEGylated
naloxone) for opioid-induced constipation (OIC). Al-Huniti 2016 analysed the
two identical phase III studies KODIAC 4 and KODIAC 5 with two separately
fitted models: a longitudinal ordered-categorical Markov model of the daily
number of spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs), and a time-to-event model of
diary entry discontinuation (DED). The paper then combined the two by
simulation to predict the protocol responder rate. Both models use the
naloxegol **dose**; individual predicted concentrations from the population PK
model did not improve the fit (Supplementary Table S3), so no PK model is
needed.

# Population

1,331 adults in the intention-to-treat population of KODIAC 4 (NCT01309841)
and KODIAC 5 (NCT01323790), randomized to placebo or naloxegol 12.5 or 25 mg
once daily for 12 weeks after a 2-week OIC confirmation (baseline) period
(Table 1). All took stable maintenance opioids (30-1000 mg/day oral morphine
equivalents) for noncancer pain and reported fewer than 3 SBMs per week. Mean
age was 52 years, 62% were women, about 79% were White and 19% Black, and the
mean baseline SBM frequency was 1.3-1.6 per week by arm. About two thirds took
a strong opioid at baseline. The SBM analysis used 108,051 daily diary entries
(day -13 to day 84); the DED analysis used day 0 to day 84.

The correlations printed in the upper triangle of the Table S4 random-effects
matrix (0.467, -0.324, -0.423, -0.0332, -0.145, -0.140) are reproduced from the
packaged variances and covariances to within rounding.

```{r models}
mod_sbm <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_sbm"))
mod_ded <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("AlHuniti_2016_naloxegol_ded"))

om <- mod_sbm$omega
round(cov2cor(om), 3)
```

# Typical-value checks

## Threshold probabilities

For a typical patient (all random effects zero) the model gives the
probability of each daily SBM count in each period. In the baseline period
the probability of four or more SBMs is effectively zero, by construction.

```{r typical-probs}
typ <- expand.grid(
  time = c(-1, 84),
  PDV = c(0, 1),
  DOSE = c(0, 12.5, 25),
  OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY = 0
) |>
  filter(!(time < 0 & DOSE > 0)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), evid = 0)

typ_sim <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_sbm), typ, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(
    period = ifelse(time > 0, "treatment (day 84)", "baseline"),
    PDV = typ$PDV,
    DOSE = typ$DOSE
  )

typ_sim |>
  select(period, PDV, DOSE, p0, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, sbm_mean) |>
  mutate(across(p0:sbm_mean, \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename("Previous-day SBM" = PDV, "Dose (mg)" = DOSE, "Mean SBM/day" = sbm_mean) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Probabilities sum to one in every stratum.
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(typ_sim[, paste0("p", 0:6)]) - 1) < 1e-10))
```

## Non-drug effect plateau

The placebo effect rises with half-life exp(2.92) = 18.5 days and is 97% of
its plateau of 0.189 logit units by day 93, the "five half-lives" quoted in the
Results.

```{r nd-plateau}
nd <- data.frame(id = 1, time = c(1, 19.5, 93), evid = 0, PDV = 0, DOSE = 0, OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY = 0)
nd_sim <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_sbm), nd, returnType = "data.frame")
nd_sim[, c("time", "fnd")]
stopifnot(
  abs(nd_sim$fnd[1]) < 1e-12,
  abs(nd_sim$fnd[2] - 0.189 / 2) < 1e-3,
  abs(nd_sim$fnd[3] / 0.189 - (1 - 2^-5)) < 0.01
)
```

## Diary entry discontinuation against the closed-form survival

The DED model has no random effects, so its survival is deterministic. The
packaged ODE solution matches direct numerical integration of the published
hazard, and the day-84 DED rates are compared with the population simulations
of Table 3 (which also sampled parameter uncertainty).

```{r ded-check}
ded_ev <- expand.grid(id = 1:3, time = c(0, seq(1, 84, by = 1))) |>
  mutate(DOSE = c(0, 12.5, 25)[id], evid = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time)
ded_sim <- rxSolve(mod_ded, ded_ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(DOSE = ded_ev$DOSE)

ded_closed <- function(base, slp, end = 1.08, tmax = 84) {
  h <- function(t) exp(base + slp * t + ifelse(t >= 80, end * (t - 80), 0))
  cumh <- integrate(h, 0, min(tmax, 80))$value
  if (tmax > 80) cumh <- cumh + integrate(h, 80, tmax)$value
  exp(-cumh)
}
ded_tab <- tibble(
  arm = c("Placebo", "Naloxegol 12.5 mg/day", "Naloxegol 25 mg/day"),
  DOSE = c(0, 12.5, 25),
  closed = c(ded_closed(-6.28, 0.00970), ded_closed(-6.18, 0.00818), ded_closed(-5.54, -0.00114)),
  published = c(42.0, 41.9, 43.4)
) |>
  left_join(ded_sim |> filter(time == 84) |> select(DOSE, sur), by = "DOSE") |>
  mutate(simulated = 100 * (1 - sur))

stopifnot(all(abs(ded_tab$sur - ded_tab$closed) < 1e-5))
# The typical-value DED rate sits within 3 percentage points of the
# uncertainty-propagated population mean in Table 3.
stopifnot(all(abs(ded_tab$simulated - ded_tab$published) < 3))

ded_tab |>
  select(arm, simulated, published) |>
  mutate(simulated = round(simulated, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment group" = arm,
    "Model DED rate by day 84 (%)" = simulated,
    "Table 3 DED rate (%)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r ded-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(ded_sim, aes(time, sur, colour = factor(DOSE))) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "Fraction providing diary entries",
    colour = "Naloxegol (mg/day)",
    title = "Diary entry discontinuation survival by arm",
    caption = "Compare with the simulated bands of Figure 4 of Al-Huniti 2016."
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 1))
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The SBM model is a first-order Markov model: the threshold logits depend on
whether the patient had at least one SBM on the previous day (`PDV`). To
simulate it, the model is solved once per subject with every day duplicated,
one row with `PDV = 0` and one with `PDV = 1`, so each subject's random
effects are shared across both rows. The daily count is then drawn in R,
day by day, from the row that matches the count drawn the day before.

Each cohort has 200 patients. Figure 2 of the paper separates patients who
did and did not use strong opioids at baseline, so the cohorts below are one
per dose and opioid group. The responder-rate cohorts mix the groups with 34%
weak-opioid-only patients, the share implied by the widths of the observed
confidence intervals in Table 2 (about 155 of 443 placebo and 140 of 440
naloxegol 12.5 mg patients).

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160701)
set.seed(20160701)
n_per <- 200
days <- -13:84

make_events <- function(n, dose, weak, id0 = 0) {
  base <- expand.grid(id = id0 + seq_len(n), time = days, PDV = c(0, 1))
  base |>
    mutate(
      evid = 0,
      DOSE = ifelse(time > 0, dose, 0),
      OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY = weak[id - id0]
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, PDV)
}

simulate_sbm <- function(n, dose, weak, label, id0 = 0) {
  ev <- make_events(n, dose, weak, id0)
  sim <- rxSolve(mod_sbm, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(sim) == nrow(ev))
  sim$PDV <- ev$PDV
  pcols <- paste0("p", 0:6)
  # cumulative probabilities, one matrix per PDV state, rows = (id, day)
  cum0 <- t(apply(as.matrix(sim[sim$PDV == 0, pcols]), 1, cumsum))
  cum1 <- t(apply(as.matrix(sim[sim$PDV == 1, pcols]), 1, cumsum))
  nd <- length(days)
  counts <- matrix(NA_integer_, n, nd)
  prev <- rep(0L, n)
  for (j in seq_len(nd)) {
    rows <- (seq_len(n) - 1) * nd + j
    cp <- ifelse(prev > 0, 1, 0) * cum1[rows, , drop = FALSE] +
      ifelse(prev > 0, 0, 1) * cum0[rows, , drop = FALSE]
    u <- runif(n)
    counts[, j] <- rowSums(u > cp)
    prev <- counts[, j]
  }
  tibble(
    id = rep(id0 + seq_len(n), times = nd),
    day = rep(days, each = n),
    sbm = as.vector(counts),
    group = label,
    DOSE = dose,
    OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY = rep(weak, times = nd)
  )
}

fig2_groups <- expand.grid(DOSE = c(0, 12.5, 25), OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY = c(0, 1))
fig2 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig2_groups)), function(i) {
  simulate_sbm(
    n_per, fig2_groups$DOSE[i], rep(fig2_groups$OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY[i], n_per),
    label = paste0(fig2_groups$DOSE[i], " mg"), id0 = (i - 1) * n_per
  )
}))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: mean SBMs per week by dose and baseline opioid potency

```{r fig2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
weekly <- fig2 |>
  mutate(week = ifelse(day <= 0, ifelse(day <= -7, -2, -1), ceiling(day / 7))) |>
  group_by(DOSE, OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY, id, week) |>
  summarise(sbm_week = sum(sbm) * 7 / n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(DOSE, OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY, week) |>
  summarise(mean_sbm = mean(sbm_week), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(opioid = ifelse(OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY == 1, "Not using strong opioids", "Using strong opioids"))

ggplot(weekly, aes(week, mean_sbm, colour = opioid)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~DOSE, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Mean number of SBM per week", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Al-Huniti 2016 (one simulated cohort of 200 per panel and group)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Figure 2 of the paper (population means with parameter uncertainty) shows
about 1.4 SBMs per week at baseline and, at week 12, about 3.5 per week on
placebo, 4.4 (strong opioids) and 3.75 (weak only) on 12.5 mg, and 4.85 and
3.9 on 25 mg. These values were read from the figure by the maintainers.

```{r fig2-compare}
fig2_ref <- tribble(
  ~DOSE, ~OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY, ~week, ~published,
  0, 0, 12, 3.5,
  0, 1, 12, 3.5,
  12.5, 0, 12, 4.4,
  12.5, 1, 12, 3.75,
  25, 0, 12, 4.85,
  25, 1, 12, 3.9
)
fig2_cmp <- weekly |>
  inner_join(fig2_ref, by = c("DOSE", "OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY", "week")) |>
  mutate(simulated = round(mean_sbm, 2))
fig2_cmp |>
  select(DOSE, opioid, simulated, published) |>
  rename(
    "Dose (mg/day)" = DOSE, "Baseline opioids" = opioid,
    "Simulated week-12 mean SBM/week" = simulated,
    "Figure 2 (digitised)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

base_mean <- weekly |> filter(week < 0) |> pull(mean_sbm)
stopifnot(
  # Baseline frequency of Table 1 (1.3-1.6 per week by arm).
  abs(median(base_mean) - 1.4) < 0.3,
  # Cohort means of 200 patients carry a Monte Carlo SD of roughly 0.25.
  median(abs(fig2_cmp$mean_sbm - fig2_cmp$published)) < 0.5
)
```

## Responder rate (Tables 2 and 3)

A responder had at least 3 SBMs per week and an increase of at least 1 SBM
per week over baseline in at least 9 of the 12 treatment weeks, and in at
least 3 of the final 4 weeks. Days on or after a patient's diary entry
discontinuation, drawn from the DED model, carry no diary entries, so they
contribute no SBMs to their week.

```{r responder}
draw_ded <- function(n, dose) {
  surv <- ded_sim |> filter(DOSE == dose)
  u <- runif(n)
  # Survival falls monotonically, so invert it on the daily grid; a draw below
  # the day-84 survival means no discontinuation within the study.
  t_ded <- approx(rev(surv$sur), rev(surv$time), xout = u)$y
  ifelse(u < min(surv$sur), Inf, t_ded)
}

resp_cohorts <- lapply(seq_along(c(0, 12.5, 25)), function(i) {
  dose <- c(0, 12.5, 25)[i]
  weak <- rbinom(n_per, 1, 0.34)
  s <- simulate_sbm(n_per, dose, weak, label = paste0(dose, " mg"), id0 = 10000 + (i - 1) * n_per)
  ded <- tibble(id = 10000 + (i - 1) * n_per + seq_len(n_per), t_ded = draw_ded(n_per, dose))
  s |> left_join(ded, by = "id")
})

resp_daily <- bind_rows(resp_cohorts) |>
  mutate(sbm_obs = ifelse(day > 0 & day >= t_ded, 0L, sbm))

resp_base <- resp_daily |>
  filter(day <= 0) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(baseline_week = sum(sbm_obs) / 2, .groups = "drop")

responder <- resp_daily |>
  filter(day > 0) |>
  mutate(week = ceiling(day / 7)) |>
  group_by(DOSE, OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY, id, week) |>
  summarise(sbm_week = sum(sbm_obs), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(resp_base, by = "id") |>
  mutate(resp_week = sbm_week >= 3 & sbm_week >= baseline_week + 1) |>
  group_by(DOSE, OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY, id) |>
  summarise(
    responder = sum(resp_week) >= 9 & sum(resp_week[week >= 9]) >= 3,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

resp_tab <- responder |>
  group_by(DOSE) |>
  summarise(simulated = 100 * mean(responder), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    placebo_adjusted = simulated - simulated[DOSE == 0],
    published = c(33.2, 43.5, 44.2),
    published_adjusted = c(NA, 10.4, 11.1)
  )
resp_tab |>
  mutate(across(c(simulated, placebo_adjusted), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Dose (mg/day)" = DOSE,
    "Simulated responder rate (%)" = simulated,
    "Simulated placebo-adjusted (%)" = placebo_adjusted,
    "Table 3 responder rate (%)" = published,
    "Table 3 placebo-adjusted (%)" = published_adjusted
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

responder |>
  group_by(DOSE, OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY) |>
  summarise(n = n(), simulated = round(100 * mean(responder), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(opioid = ifelse(OPIOID_WEAK_ONLY == 1, "Weak only", "Strong (or weak + strong)")) |>
  select(DOSE, opioid, n, simulated) |>
  rename(
    "Dose (mg/day)" = DOSE, "Baseline opioids" = opioid, "N" = n,
    "Simulated responder rate (%)" = simulated
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# 200 patients per arm give a binomial SD of about 3.4 percentage points.
stopifnot(abs(median(resp_tab$simulated - resp_tab$published)) < 6)
```

Table 2 reports model-predicted responder rates of 33.0 / 32.9% (placebo,
weak / strong opioids), 36.5 / 45.6% (12.5 mg) and 35.8 / 46.2% (25 mg): the
treatment benefit lies in the patients taking strong opioids, as above.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Errata.** A Europe PMC search on 2026-11-24 found no erratum or
  correction for this article.
* **Two model files, one paper.** The SBM and DED models were fitted
  separately (different datasets, different control streams) and are packaged
  as two files; the paper's responder-rate prediction combines them by
  simulation, as done above.
* **Markov state supplied as data.** The previous-day SBM count is a data
  column (`PDV`, source `PDVORD`) exactly as in the control stream, which keeps
  the model fittable. Simulation must update it from the previously drawn
  count, which this vignette does in R. The paper dropped each patient's first
  record (no previous day); the simulation above starts day -13 from
  `PDV = 0`.
* **Dose during the baseline period.** The control stream applies
  `FD = EMAX * DOSE / (ED50 + DOSE)` on every record. The packaged model
  assumes, as the analysis dataset must have, that `DOSE` is 0 for all
  baseline-period days and for placebo.
* **Baseline thresholds 4-6.** The control stream fixes the baseline-period
  decrements for thresholds 4-6 at 20 logit units rather than estimating them;
  they are hard-coded in `model()` the same way.
* **Day-80 switch in the DED hazard.** The paper defines the end-of-study
  indicator as 1 for times at or after day 80. The control stream evaluates
  it in `$PK` at each daily record, so NONMEM applies it over the whole
  interval ending at day 80; the packaged model switches it on continuously at
  day 80. The day-84 DED rate differs by less than 0.1 percentage point.
* **25 mg DED time slope.** Supplementary Table S6 prints -0.00114 for the
  25 mg time slope, while the model-building summary (Table S5, run 3, the
  same run and objective function value) prints -0.00143. The packaged model
  uses the final-estimate table (S6); the alternative changes the 25 mg
  day-84 DED rate from 42.0% to 41.5%.
* **Responder computation.** The paper does not state how incomplete weeks
  were handled. Here a day after diary entry discontinuation contributes no
  SBMs to its week. The paper's population simulations (Table 3) also sampled
  parameter uncertainty by a smoothed bootstrap, which this vignette does not
  do, and used 2,000 patients per arm against 200 here.
* **Opioid potency mix.** The share of weak-opioid-only patients (34%) is
  derived from the confidence-interval widths of the observed responder rates
  in Table 2; the paper reports only that about two thirds took strong opioids.
* **Placeholder residual on DED survival.** The DED model exposes the survival
  probability `sur` with a fixed additive SD of 0.001 so that nlmixr2 accepts
  it; the paper's likelihood is the time-to-event likelihood of its control
  stream.
* **No PKNCA.** Both models are dose-driven exposure-response models with no
  concentration output, so the noncompartmental analysis section of the
  standard template does not apply.
